Drex Max is its most capable decision model, and it now runs on your own hardware. The release ships bf16 weights, a Q8_0 GGUF , an affine Q4 checkpoint and forks of llama.cpp and Ollama . For developers, Drex Max open weights mean routing, classification and policy checks can stay on a local machine. Best: 97.3 skill on InfographicVQA. Tools area reaches 81.9. A top-tier decision model you can now run offline on a Mac. What is Drex Max? Drex Max is a decision model from Nace.AI that answers typed questions about a given context. You pass a state (text, JSON or images) plus named questions. The model returns a probability for every option in one forward pass. Nothing is generated . Questions come in 3 types: choice among named options, yes/no, and an ordinal score. That makes it a fit for agent routing, ticket triage and guardrail checks. The hosted version is presented at routing, classification and policy checks. How does Drex Max work? The model card describes a dense 27B backbone with 64 layers. 48 are Gated DeltaNet linear-attention layers that run left to right. The other 16 are full-attention layers, placed every fourth layer, and they are non-causal. Every token can attend to the whole sequence. Images pass through a native vision tower and are visible to every question in a request. A 255-way readout head then turns the last hidden state into option probabilities. The config lists a qwen3_5 model type with a 262,144-position window. How does Drex Max perform on benchmarks? All figures below are self-reported by Nace AI, Decision Index 0.4 (public text): 67.52.
